evidence: Plans/human-in-the-loop.md:2653 locates the file at “`<project root>/.puppet-master/PAUSE.md`”, specifies pause_id, scope, reason, created_by, created_at_utc, optional expires_at_utc and allowed_action_ids[], and says “Evaluate PAUSE first. For an action that passes PAUSE, evaluate any required HITL approval before dispatch.” Plans/orchestrator-subagent-integration.md:29203–29206 makes the check live. Its Pause Gate Live Contract at 35242–35247 says the Orchestrator reads the file “before dispatching each new execution-unit attempt” and “before admitting `cmd.orchestrator.resume`”. An invalid file pauses project-wide with an empty allowlist. An in-scope halted run can resume after removal or expiry.

regressions.what: The new stale-target recovery instruction directs the user to “run `Revalidate target` first”. ACD-100 already listed that label only where supported. The catalog and production matrix wire Open target and the Debug target picker, but assign no command or explicit view-local action to the Revalidate target control. evidence: The deferred-action finding points to the same file as row 1501. Both Plans/human-in-the-loop.md:2653 and Plans/orchestrator-subagent-integration.md:35242 now say “`<project root>/.puppet-master/PAUSE.md`”. The latter adds “no other path is read”. OSI-387 specifies “This per-dispatch check is the live pause-gate watcher” (29204). The live contract gives the pre-attempt and resume admission checks, project/run scope, exact action allowlist, invalid-file handling and the clear condition “only when the file is removed or expires” (35243–35247). HITL gives the frontmatter fields and requires “any required HITL approval before dispatch” after the PAUSE check. The earlier Rust iteration snippet is no longer the sole watcher specification.

Plans/agent-rules-context.md:80, 2430 binds every caller to “get_agent_rules_context(request: &AgentRulesContextRequest) -> AgentRulesContextResult” and makes the consumer rule clear: “the result is usable if and only if `errors[]` is empty”. A missing Project rules file yields a usable warning. A read error clears formatted_block_ref, sets byte_count to zero and refuses dispatch. The two budget outcomes depend on “bytes over the warn threshold, non-strict” versus “strict mode is on and the block is still over `max_bytes` after truncation”. The typed request ends with “`scoped_agents_enabled` boolean; `max_bytes` integer, at least 1; `created_at_utc` string (RFC 3339 UTC)”. Its named revisions cover rule sources, and it says “The pipeline reads exactly the named revisions and never substitutes a newer one” (2431). ARC-029 requires strict-mode blocking but does not supply the mode to this function (1979–1981).
missing: Bind the effective strict-mode decision and warn threshold to the call, either as resolved request values or through an identified policy source. For a block still over budget after truncation, the written function contract cannot determine which of the warning-only and dispatch-refusing outcomes applies from its declared inputs.

regressions.what: The replacement for the illustrative application_config argument is now the only supported request, but it carries max_bytes without an effective strictness value or a specified lookup for that value. The new API can represent both budget outcomes in its result yet omits the input that selects between them.
